plans.name: Free
plans.bestFor: Trying it out, or asking a few questions here and there.
plans.notes: Unlimited plain text chats using the everyday model (GPT-5.6 Luna). Picture making, file sending, voice and research are all capped. The Sora help page states Free accounts are not eligible for video generation.

plans.name: Go
plans.bestFor: Someone who uses it most days but doesn't need the smartest answers.
plans.notes: Price confirmed by OpenAI: "In the US, Go is available for $8 per month." Marked uncertain because two values could not be confirmed on an official page: OpenAI's Sora help article lists Plus, Team and Pro as eligible for video making and does not mention Go, so video_generation is left blank rather than guessed; the same applies to priority access at busy times, which OpenAI only states for Plus and above. Go uses the same everyday model as Free (GPT-5.6 Luna) and does not get GPT-5.6 Sol.

plans.name: Plus
plans.bestFor: Most people who use it every day for work, study or writing.
plans.notes: OpenAI states "$20/month (billed monthly)". Adds the harder-thinking model (GPT-5.6 Sol at Medium and High thinking), projects, scheduled tasks, custom GPTs and expanded Codex coding use. No annual price is published.

plans.name: Pro ($100)
plans.bestFor: People who use it for many hours a day and need the strongest answers.
plans.notes: OpenAI now sells Pro as two tiers. Its help center says: "Pro $100 unlocks 5x higher usage than Plus, while Pro $200 unlocks 20x usage than Plus." Both Pro tiers include the same features; only the amount of use differs. Adds GPT-6 Pro (powered by GPT-6 Astra) and every thinking level of GPT-5.6 Sol.

plans.name: Pro ($200)
plans.bestFor: Very heavy users who keep running out of room on the $100 Pro tier.
plans.notes: Same features as Pro $100. The only difference OpenAI states is the usage allowance: 20x Plus instead of 5x Plus. The feature list above cannot show that difference because both sit at the top level.

faq.q: Do I have to pay to use ChatGPT at all?
faq.a: No. The Free plan costs nothing and lets you have as many ordinary text conversations as you like. You only pay if you want more pictures, more file uploads, longer research or the smarter models.

faq.q: What happens when I run out of my monthly allowance?
faq.a: It stops letting you use that feature and tells you to wait, usually a few hours. Nothing is charged automatically. You can wait, or move up to a bigger plan.

faq.q: What is the difference between Pro at $100 and Pro at $200?
faq.a: Nothing except how much you can use. Both have exactly the same features. The $200 one simply lets you do about four times as much before you hit a limit.

faq.q: Can I cancel whenever I like?
faq.a: Yes. Paid plans are month by month. If you cancel, you keep the paid features until the end of the month you have already paid for, then drop back to Free.

notes: Checked 21 September 2026. Prices on chatgpt.com/pricing are drawn on the page by the browser and did not come through when fetched, so every price here comes from an OpenAI help-center article or an OpenAI announcement instead, which are also official sources. ChatGPT Go is confirmed available in the United States. No annual (yearly) billing option is published for any consumer tier. Model names current at the date checked: GPT-5.6 Luna (Free and Go), GPT-5.6 Sol (Plus and above), GPT-6 Astra / GPT-6 Pro (Pro only). OpenAI also sells extra usage as credits on personal plans; that is a top-up, not a plan, so it is not listed here.
